## 開篇固定收益主論述

油價連續第2天下跌、英國央行不再出售長天期公債，加上市場相信聯準會將因應通膨，使全球債券賣壓在週四暫告中斷，美國公債強勁反彈。5年期殖利率領跌10.2個基點至4.780%；10年期下跌9.2個基點至4.932%，結束連續8個交易日上升。2年期殖利率下降7.3個基點至4.665%，30年期則下降7.7個基點至5.285%。

這波反彈並未扭轉市場對貨幣政策趨緊的重新定價。聯準會週三把目標利率區間調高至3.75%-4%後，2年期殖利率本月仍累計上升近49個基點，2年與10年期利差當日再收窄1.9個基點至26.7個基點。市場真正重新區分的是短端利率進一步上升，以及央行失去對長期通膨控制這兩種風險。10年期實質殖利率下降7.1個基點至2.620%，10年期損益兩平通膨率也下降2.1個基點至2.312%。

油價回落帶來即時喘息，但能源衝擊尚未結束。沙烏地阿拉伯設法恢復東西向輸油管線的部分運能，布蘭特原油下跌1.65%至$104.08，WTI下跌1.21%至$101.19；兩者本月仍上漲逾14%，央行因此仍須留意能源成本進一步傳導至工資、食品與基礎物價。儘管如此，聯準會一致通過升息，強化了政策制定者會在衝擊持續時採取行動的信心，美債市場因而把當日油價跌勢視為足以降低通膨溢價的訊號。

美國數據使這份寬慰不那麼單純。初領失業救濟金人數意外降至19.6萬人，費城聯準銀行製造業指數仍遠高於預期，價格指標並且上升。另一方面，住宅營建轉弱，成屋待完成銷售僅微幅增加，較上年同期仍低近5%。利率敏感部門顯露疲態，有利長端殖利率下降；但勞動市場或製造業需求尚未惡化到足以中止聯準會緊縮循環。

債市內部需求也不一致。財政部增額發行$190億10年期抗通膨債券，以2.653%的實質殖利率得標，較標售前水準高約2個基點；即使名目公債上漲，標售需求仍偏弱。企業信用則較為堅挺：美國高收益債利差小幅收窄，花旗完成歷來規模最大的美元債發行，富國銀行也吸引大量訂單。標普500指數上漲1.14%，那斯達克100指數上漲1.73%，半導體類股上漲3.14%，VIX則下跌近13%。

英國是當日最明確的獨立催化因素。英國央行把政策利率維持在3.75%，若能源衝擊持續仍可能升息，但暫停主動出售公債至明年4月，並停止直接出售長天期債券；30年期英國公債殖利率下跌12個基點至5.74%。此舉移除一項長天期債券供給來源，卻未解決通膨問題，也說明為何當日債券反彈雖大，仍有條件限制：各國央行一方面在短端升息或釋出升息可能性，另一方面也設法避免資產負債表政策與政府發債不必要地加重長端壓力。

## 勞動、物價與房市訊號分歧，美債反彈

美債各期限均反彈，中期券表現最強。5年期殖利率收於4.780%，下跌10.2個基點，幅度大於10年期的9.2個基點與30年期的7.7個基點。因此，殖利率曲線延續聯準會決策所造成的政策驅動式趨平，長端並未明顯轉陡。2年與30年期利差收窄0.4個基點至62.0個基點，較1個月前趨平51.1個基點。

當日走勢部分修正了聯準會決策後的即時賣壓。央行升息25個基點原在預期之中，但主席Kevin Warsh強調通膨持續性，加上利率預測中位數顯示今年還會升息一次，週三一度把10年期殖利率推高至5.02%。週四油價走低、英國公債上漲，讓投資人轉而看到決策的另一面：即使聯準會的行動會提高短期利率預期路徑，只要央行被認為願意抑制通膨，投資人為長期物價失控所要求的補償便可下降。

利率選擇權市場也顯示，這是一場總體環境的重新定價，而非失序的美債事件。10年期利率3個月選擇權隱含的年化波動約為79.5個基點，遠低於2023年10月10年期殖利率逼近5%時的約134個基點。選擇權需求較集中於短端，反映市場對聯準會反應函數的不確定性更高。整體型態更符合經濟成長較強、預期降息次數減少及長期政策利率上升所引發的有序調整，而非美債市場功能失靈。

通膨拆解也朝有利債券的方向發展。10年期實質殖利率降至2.620%，損益兩平通膨率降至2.312%。油價走低既削弱近期通膨動能，也降低立即增持抗通膨部位的吸引力。不過，實質殖利率本月仍上升18.2個基點，名目10年期殖利率也較1個月前高20.9個基點。週四的反彈只是緩和金融狀況收緊，並未將其消除。

10年期TIPS標售呈現這項改善的界限。此次$190億增額發行以2.653%的殖利率得標，比下午1時投標截止前的交易水準高約2個基點，不但高於前次標售的2.438%，也是2008年以來最高；當年抗通膨債券曾受金融危機期間流動性壓力影響。這次需求偏弱則出現在油價下跌、投資人評估名目利率可能進一步上升之際，即使實質報酬偏高，增持抗通膨債券的急迫性仍然降低。

勞動數據幾乎未給聯準會退讓理由。截至9月12日當週，經季節調整的初領失業救濟金人數減少1萬人至19.6萬人，低於經濟學家預期的20.8萬人，並創7月中旬以來最低；4週移動平均減少2,750人至20萬3,250人。截至9月5日當週，續領人數減少3.9萬人至173萬人，低於178萬人的市場共識，也是2024年1月以來最低。季節調整扭曲可能影響數值，但方向仍顯示裁員有限，勞動市場足以承受較高利率。

費城聯準銀行調查呈現另一種韌性。9月一般商業活動指數由47.4降至37.8，但仍高於30.5的市場共識；新訂單僅由30.1小幅降至29.2，出貨指數維持在27.7。數據反映的是成長速度低於異常強勁的8月，而非經濟陷入萎縮。

就業訊號轉弱得更明顯。調查中的就業指數下跌16點至11.8，資本支出指數由48.2降至37.1，未來一般商業活動指數下降21點至52.9。這些數值削弱成長訊號，但仍處於正值，距離通常足以結束緊縮循環的全面惡化仍遠。

價格壓力則朝相反方向發展。支付價格指數上升8點至48.6，收取價格指數上升14點至31.3，創4月以來最高；未來支付價格及收取價格指標分別升至71.3與72.3。認為勞動供給至少稍微限制產能的受訪者達72%，高於6月的50%；另有36%預期未來3個月能源市場限制將惡化。經濟成長放慢但仍在擴張、價格壓力反而升高，正是讓政策難以迅速轉向寬鬆的組合。

房市是當日較明確的緊縮證據。8月新屋開工下降2.6%，折合年率為127.5萬戶，低於131萬戶的市場共識，前值則修正為130.9萬戶。建築許可下降2.7%至139.4萬戶，低於預期的141萬戶與前值143.3萬戶。新屋開工已接近疫情以來最低水準，多戶住宅營建是主要拖累。

8月成屋待完成銷售上升0.3%，是5月以來首次增加，也優於彭博調查預期的下降0.1%；但增幅低於Trading Economics另行報導的2%市場共識，尚不足以顯示房市全面復甦。簽約量較上年同期下降4.7%，前次降幅為2.2%。南部與西部銷售上升，中西部與東北部則下降。

融資條件仍是這種分歧的主因。美國30年期房貸平均利率由6.76%升至6.95%，15年期房貸利率由6.09%升至6.26%。即使借款成本偏高，買方不再等待利率下降時，待完成交易仍可能增加；但接近7%的房貸利率對負擔能力與建案經濟效益的限制，仍反映在年增率疲弱及營建下滑上。

這批數據沒有給聯準會單一的總體政策指引。失業救濟申請與製造業價格支持央行繼續保持警戒；新屋開工、建築許可及工廠就業轉弱，則顯示緊縮已在傳導。美債反彈正反映這項雙面結果：市場下調了每逢強勁數據便須立即再升息的機率，但政策仍須因應持續性通膨與韌性勞動需求的大方向並未改變。

## 英國撤除長天期公債供給，仍維持升息傾向

英國央行連續第6次會議把銀行利率維持在3.75%，貨幣政策委員會9名成員中有6人支持按兵不動。Catherine Mann、Megan Greene與首席經濟學家Huw Pill主張立即升息，延續7月的6比3票數。3人認為，在能源成本上升傳導至2027年初薪資協議前採取行動，可降低政策落後於通膨的風險。

總裁Andrew Bailey及多數委員判斷，全球能源衝擊目前對英國國內物價與工資的影響有限，但這份容忍有其條件。Bailey表示，波動持續愈久，通膨影響就愈大，升息的可能性也愈高。委員會認為通膨風險比7月更加偏向上行，並預期明年初物價漲幅將達2%目標的約兩倍。

英國央行同時承認經濟活動較強。近期數據優於預期後，央行把第3季成長估計調高至0.4%。這份韌性降低再升息的即時成長代價，但委員會也指出勞動市場仍有閒置、薪資成長減速，失業率接近5%。因此，本次決策雖維持緊縮傾向，卻未認同能源驅動的本週賣壓最嚴重時，市場曾反映的5次各25個基點升息。

更大的市場意外來自資產負債表。英國央行計畫在2034年9月前逐步處分£4,880億英國公債部位，但已暫停所有主動出售至2027年4月，並停止直接出售長天期債券。2035年至2049年到期的公債，未來可能移交債務管理局，而非由央行直接在市場出售，最終仍待財政部決定。

提案大致把投資組合分為三部分：約£2,220億在2035年前到期的債券將自然到期；英國央行將保留約£1,200億於2049年或之後到期的公債，作為流通紙鈔的資產支持；其餘£1,460億於2035年至2049年到期的債券，則可移交債務管理局，或由該局以每年約£200億的速度出售。債務管理局更有彈性，可把流動性較差的債券替換為更符合投資人需求的指標年期。

這項改變處理了長端持續承壓的一項來源。英國央行估計，量化緊縮已使10年期政府借款成本增加20至30個基點；民間估計則認為，其對30年期殖利率的影響更大。退休基金對超長天期債券的需求已經減弱，政府本身發債規模又大，使市場更難吸收央行直接出售的部位。

30年期英國公債殖利率在近期觸及1998年以來最高後，下跌12個基點至5.74%，創5月以來最大跌幅；2年期殖利率下降6個基點至4.70%。交易員把11月升息機率下調至約85%，對未來1年的定價則降至不到4次升息。

這波漲勢不代表資產負債表政策的紓解已解決英國通膨問題。英國央行預期嚴重聖嬰現象將推升食品價格，使能源衝擊雪上加霜，並警告間接效應可能只是延後出現，而非不存在。政府明年1月重設能源價格上限，將把批發成本傳導給家庭，時點又與年度薪資協議重疊。3名異議委員正因這項時程，主張應在第二輪效應浮現前採取行動。

政策利率決策與公債供給決策各有不同目的。利率不變可保留觀察國內傳導的時間，暫停售債則降低一項可以避免的長端壓力。英國央行並未啟動新的資產購買計畫來壓低借款成本，也未放棄縮減投資組合；它只是改變退場方式與年期組成，同時保留在能源與食品通膨擴散時升息的選項。

財政部仍須決定是否接受把債券移交債務管理局的提案。若付諸實施，公共債務銷售將集中於最能選擇流動性指標債券並調整期限的機構，週四的長端紓解因而可能比短期暫停售債更持久。不過，政府財政展望與整體借款需求仍是彼此獨立的英國公債供給來源。

## 信用市場消化銀行與AI融資

企業債市與美債、股市同步走強。高收益債利差小幅收窄，經配息調整後的主要基金總報酬均為正值：LQD上漲約0.68%、HYG上漲0.38%、JNK上漲0.37%、EMB上漲0.64%。這顯示債市漲勢獲得廣泛參與，並非只集中於政府債券的利率部位。

花旗趁市場改善籌得$120億，創下該行歷來最大規模的美元債發行。訂單峰值約$400億，相當於最終發行規模的約3.3倍，其中最長年期券種的需求就達約$180億。11年期債券的定價利差由初步討論的較指標利率高約125個基點，收窄至93個基點。

這筆交易使花旗今年美元債發行額增至$183億。美國6大銀行今年已在投資級債市合計籌得$1,773億，以高盛的$440億居首。富國銀行週四也發行$60億4年期與11年期債券，峰值訂單約$280億。

在美債絕對殖利率仍高的情況下，訂單簿如此強勁格外值得注意。借款人受惠於當日政府債券上漲及信用風險溢價收窄，投資人取得的整體殖利率則仍遠高於低利率時期。長年期銀行債需求尤其強勁，因許多企業發行人不願把偏高的融資成本鎖定數十年，這類債券供給已變得稀少。

AI基礎設施持續帶來更複雜的融資安排。CoreWeave推出一筆2033年到期、規模$30億的可轉換公司債，另有把交易擴大$5億的選擇權，初步討論票息區間為2.375%-2.875%。公司也設立隨市發行計畫，可出售最多3,500萬股股票。

這項組合讓CoreWeave同時取得債務與股權連結資金，並把部分投資報酬轉由公司未來股價提供，使近期現金票息低於傳統無擔保債務。募集資金將用於一般公司用途，其中一部分用來支付與可轉債發行相關的衍生性金融商品。

CoreWeave發債之際，美國上市公司今年透過可轉債籌資已創下$1,373億紀錄。資料中心、晶片與電力連線成本超過任何單一融資管道能承擔的規模，使AI相關發行人廣泛使用可轉債、槓桿貸款、私募債及資產擔保架構。今年全球AI基礎設施相關企業已借款約$4,190億，投資人疲態也開始出現；CoreWeave在7月便須改善一筆$26億槓桿貸款的條件。

CleanSpark則測試較傳統的高收益債管道。公司尋求透過首次發行5年期垃圾債籌得約$22.3億，用於喬治亞州Sandersville的一座資料中心。初步討論殖利率約8.5%，比彭博追蹤的BB級債券平均殖利率高約2個百分點。交易推出時，訂單規模大致只與發行額相當，需求遠不及銀行債數倍超額認購的程度。

該項目已依一份為期20年、總值$66億的合約全數出租給Meta子公司Anviran；預期Meta將擔保租金與營運費用，資料中心則預定於2027年第4季開始營運。這項承諾提供長期收入來源，但債券持有人仍須承擔營建風險、營運前的等待期，以及一家市值約$32.9億公司的融資需求。

這是首筆與Meta資料中心相關的垃圾債發行。今年開發商已出售約$390億高收益債，多數以Amazon、Oracle等大型科技公司的租約作為支持。約8.5%的初步殖利率顯示，超大規模雲端業者的合約收入雖能協助取得市場融資，卻無法消除施工階段垃圾級項目所需支付的溢酬。

當日各筆交易的差異清楚反映市場取捨。花旗與富國銀行是擁有流動性良好殖利率曲線的成熟銀行，因而吸引深厚需求；CoreWeave讓投資人參與股價上漲，以降低現金票息；CleanSpark則仰賴一份特定長期租約，仍須支付明顯較高的殖利率。信用市場保持開放，但條件取決於借款人、擔保品、施工狀態及現金流形成路徑，不能一概解讀為市場熱烈追捧AI融資。

## 私募債壓力暴露衡量與估值落差

私募信貸呈現較不樂觀的景象，但壓力規模高度取決於如何定義違約。惠譽估計違約率創紀錄達6.3%；Houlihan Lokey按貸款規模加權後得到低於1%的比率，因最大型借款人仍正常履約；Pimco針對商業發展公司所採用、範圍更廣的「影子」違約率則達19%，高於2022年的約14%。

這些數字衡量的母體與事件並不相同。有些方法只計入未付款或正式重整，另一些則納入延長到期日，以及放款後為紓解現金流壓力而增加的以債付息（PIK）債務。Pimco把這類「不良PIK」列入計算，理由是以新增債務取代現金利息，即使貸款在技術上仍維持正常，也可能掩蓋財務惡化。

在一個規模達$1.8兆、缺乏全面產業資料庫的市場，這種落差格外重要。Lincoln International追蹤的歐洲私募貸款違約率為1.5%，部分原因是其口徑排除了其他衡量方式納入的某些重整案件。按貸款規模加權，也會壓低小型借款人的影響，而壓力正較集中於這些公司。

投資人要問的不只是何種數字正確，也包括損失與展期是否已大到足以侵蝕報酬。一項業界估計認為，對高槓桿企業放款的管理人可承受8%-9%的違約率；重大衝擊後若逼近12%-15%，則可能引發系統性疑慮。除整體違約件數外，回收價值、擔保品品質，以及利息究竟有多少真正以現金支付，同樣重要。

Bathla Group具體呈現估值不確定性。Centuria Bass Credit曾探詢出售部分與這家無力償債的澳洲建商相關的債務，但交易尚未接近成交，潛在買方要求至少20%-30%的折價。Centuria Bass先前揭露對Bathla有A$2.78億曝險，以6個住宅開發案作為擔保；外界審視升高後，公司並暫停兩檔基金的贖回。

Bathla積欠債權人約A$34億，其中多數債權屬於私募信貸基金。公司因難以償債，已於8月進入自願管理程序；管理人取得約A$400萬緊急融資，並正尋求規模更大的方案。此案對澳洲A$2,000億私募信貸產業尤其重要，因約半數資產與房地產開發相關，而高利率、營建成本及銷售疲弱可同時侵蝕現金流與擔保品價值。

債權人也對企業盈餘的衡量方式提出質疑。法國物業服務公司Emeria把未來AI計畫預期節省的€2,000萬，加入過去12個月EBITDA。投資人、律師及分析師表示，這是他們首次看到公司以這種方式計入尚未實現的AI效益。

Emeria表示，調整項目來自已識別的措施，包括文件自動製作、客戶服務、會計與後台作業。這筆金額未經查核，也未由公司獨立會計師檢視，仍可能變動。由於公司約有€35億債務、盈餘正在萎縮且到期日逼近，這項差別相當重要。

Emeria以備考淨負債與調整後EBITDA計算，申報槓桿倍數約8.44倍。若排除AI項目及其他合計約€4,000萬的調整，彭博計算的倍數約為9.3倍。債務協商持續之際，贊助股東正考慮可能注資€3.5億。因此，爭議不只關乎會計表達：把節省金額視為已實現盈餘，會直接改變市場用來判斷再融資能力的槓桿指標。

Braskem的重整協商則顯示，估值爭議可以迅速演變為新資金與控制權之爭。在這家巴西石化公司持續處理$110億債務之際，債券持有人拒絕了最新方案。該方案要求債權人提供約$20億新融資，其中約$12.5億用來以低至面額50%的價格回購既有債務，其餘$7.5億則支應營運資金。

債權人反對在股東Petrobras與IG4 Capital未提出具法律約束力的出資承諾前提供新資金。Petrobras希望避免公司聲請破產，卻尚未承諾債券持有人要求的具約束力股權支持。部分債權人甚至考慮完全不提出反方案，使司法重整重新成為協商核心。

各方須在10月9日前就條款清單達成協議，並於11月底前提出獲過半債權人支持的最終計畫。Braskem於2030年到期的美元債殖利率約26%，反映協商可能進入法院程序。爭議的核心是損失如何實質分配：債權人不但要提供流動性，也要出資折價回購債務，股東卻尚未保證相應注資。

這些案件共同揭露數種隱藏槓桿。以債付息重整可延後正式認列違約；私募貸款在實際嘗試出售前可能沒有可觀察市價；預期AI節省可在效益實現前墊高盈餘；重整方案也可把債權人的資金稱為救援資本，卻不先釐清股東應承擔的責任。公開市場發債熱絡、整體利差偏緊，並未消除這些個別借款人的弱點。

## 全球政策與主權融資仍偏緊

印度央行完成流動性回收計畫的第一批交易，而該計畫先前已使本地殖利率曲線承壓。印度儲備銀行出售5,000億盧比、約$52億的政府債券，於2029至2032財政年度到期。這是RBI自2017年11月以來首次透過標售進行公開市場債券淨賣出。

標售截止殖利率略高於市場預估。結果公布後，5年期殖利率一度上升6個基點至6.83%，指標10年期殖利率最多上升3個基點。相對走勢反映操作集中在對銀行體系流動性敏感的年期，也反映市場預期10月將升息。

這次售債回收的資金接近銀行體系存款的0.2%。過剩流動性在9月6日曾創11.6兆盧比紀錄，之後經由稅款繳納與外匯干預降至約7.4兆盧比。RBI計畫於9月21日及28日再進行兩次各2,500億盧比的售債，完成已宣布的1兆盧比方案。ICICI Securities Primary Dealership估計，整個緊縮循環最終可能透過售債回收約2兆盧比。

印度央行在抽離現金的同時增加債券供給，使這項操作的影響大於暫時性流動性工具。交易員普遍預期10月升息25個基點，油價高於$100也增加輸入性通膨壓力。這項結果強化全球央行同時運用政策利率與資產負債表抗通膨的格局；英國央行則反向調整資產負債表退場方式，以減輕對長端的干擾。

捷克央行在6月進行4年來首次升息後，一致決議把指標利率維持在3.75%。總裁Ales Michl表示，先前升息目前已充分收緊金融狀況，但下次會議仍可能在再升息與維持不變之間選擇。核心通膨仍偏高，官員正在觀察服務、住房、工資、政府支出與油價。

遠期利率市場反映年底前還會升息兩次、每次25個基點，未來12個月合計升息4次。Michl並未認同這條路徑，但表示若通膨風險成真，決策委員會將再次收緊政策。因此，即使8月整體通膨低於目標，11月會議仍存在採取行動的可能。

歐洲央行的公開辯論同樣聚焦於：尚未造成工資物價螺旋的能源衝擊，是否仍會要求央行進一步行動。愛爾蘭央行總裁Gabriel Makhlouf表示，每次會議都有採取行動的可能，包括10月29日會議。他尚未看到令人擔憂的工資傳導，但強調通膨仍高於ECB的2%目標，能源風險也仍偏向上行。

芬蘭央行總裁Olli Rehn同樣未發現明確的第二輪效應，並指出勞動市場不如2022年緊俏；但他表示衝擊尚未結束，上行風險仍可能浮現。Rehn警告，廣泛政府補貼會削弱價格訊號，主張改採暫時且具針對性的援助。他也表示，若政治或主權市場壓力妨礙貨幣政策傳導，ECB仍可使用傳導工具，但目前不需要干預。

克羅埃西亞央行總裁Ante Zigman更強調未能壓制通膨的代價。歐元區通膨高於3%，第2季成長也強於預期；他認為物價壓力若失控，最終將危及經濟擴張。他同意工資及其他第二輪效應仍受控制，因此10月決策將取決於新數據，而非市場目前反映的至少再升息3次。

歐洲同時面臨較長期的融資問題。歐盟執委會正爭取讓歐盟共同債務更廣泛納入指數。目前流通中的歐盟債券約€8,000億，是歐洲第2大、全球第3大的AAA級債券市場。執委Valdis Dombrovskis指出，這些債券雖已在結算機構擔保品及ECB再融資操作中獲得與主權債相當的待遇，但遭主要主權債指數排除，仍限制需求與次級市場流動性。

隨著歐盟擴大發債以支應國防與下一期長期預算，納入指數可能更為重要。這項政策不會降低借款規模，卻可擴大合格投資人基礎，改善歐盟債相對於各國主權債曲線的流動性。Rehn另行支持共同發行歐洲國防債，把這項市場結構倡議與未來供給連結起來。

加拿大透過一筆2059年6月1日到期的C$30億債券標售，呈現主權融資成本上升。債券平均得標殖利率為4.201%，創2007年7月以來加拿大30年期債券標售最高水準。加拿大殖利率仍低於美國，但燃料帶動的通膨壓力與全球期限溢價上升，已推高長期借款成本。

日本則顯示吸收供給的投資人結構可能轉變。4月至9月，日本政府債券零售銷售較上年同期增加84%，創¥5.14兆紀錄。家庭持有約¥1,132兆現金與存款，政府債券僅占約1.9%；若占比回到2008年4.5%的高峰，可能帶來額外¥28.5兆購買量，相當於JGB年度發行額約22%。

日本央行減少購債、國內殖利率升高並與海外債券競爭之際，這項潛在需求相當重要。財務省計畫把零售JGB購買資格擴大至非營利機構及小型未上市公司；其他提案還包括允許政府債券納入享有稅負優惠的投資帳戶，以及讓部分持債免徵遺產稅。零售需求無法立即取代機構投資人，但在日本利率正常化之際，可提供更大的國內融資池。

新興市場主權債表現仍有選擇性，並非全面走弱。莫三比克與塞內加爾美元債本月分別回報3%與2.2%，廣泛新興市場債券指數則下跌1.23%。投資人回應莫三比克與IMF的協商、同中國進行債務重訂談判，以及債券持有人的初步接觸，使該國2031年到期歐元債殖利率9月下降76個基點至10.43%，創2022年4月以來最低。

塞內加爾尋求IMF董事會批准一項$22億計畫。官員澄清目前將繼續償付債務，並支付2048年到期債券的票息後，該國債券價格趨於穩定。兩國仍有未解決的債務可持續性問題，但在已開發市場殖利率上升之際，取得官方融資的進展仍提供了發行人特有的支撐。

## 前瞻市場意涵

日本央行9月18日決策是最近的全球政策考驗。彭博調查的所有經濟學家都預期利率將由1.00%升至1.25%，這會是3個月內第2次升息，也是1990年以來日本央行兩次升息間隔最短的一次。由於升息已幾乎完全反映在市場價格中，總裁植田和男下午3時30分的記者會將比利率決定本身提供更多訊息。

核心問題是植田會把9月行動定調為一次性加速，或保留明年1月再度升息的可能。1.25%將進入日本央行估計中性利率區間的下緣；若他繼續表示金融狀況仍然寬鬆，代表官員認為還有收緊空間。新任審議委員Asada Toichiro或Sato Ayano若提出反對，則會讓市場質疑支持升息的廣度。

聯準會升息後，日圓一度貶值1%，決策前匯率約為156日圓兌1美元。策略師認為，若日本央行溝通被解讀為偏鴿，158至158.50可能成為測試區；若美國利率上升快於日本，日後也可能觸及160。日圓投機性空頭減少，加上日美已展現聯手干預的意願，可能抑制匯率波動；但僅升息25個基點，未必足以縮小市場預期的政策利差並支撐日圓。

美國9月18日公布的工業生產與製造業產出，將把國內經濟活動測試由週四的地區製造業及房市數據進一步延伸。兩項月增率預期均由0.2%升至0.3%，產能利用率則預估由76.3%升至76.4%。結果強勁，將支持聯準會認為經濟足以承受更多緊縮的看法；若數據疲弱，則會增添新屋開工、建築許可及費城聯準銀行就業指標轉弱所提供的證據。

聯準會理事Michelle Bowman預定發表談話，將是央行一致通過升息，以及後續失業救濟申請、製造業與房市數據公布後，第一份具名的聯準會評估。市場需要判斷官員是否認同交易價格所反映的較激進路徑，或仍較接近今年再升息一次的預測中位數。短端選擇權需求顯示不確定性高於長端，這項差別對短端尤其重要。

油價仍是最即時的跨市場條件。沙烏地阿拉伯力求數日內恢復東西向輸油管線約一半運能，協助布蘭特原油收於$105以下；但WTI與布蘭特仍高於$100，中東供給也持續受限。恢復進度延誤、發生更多攻擊，或美國與伊朗緊張再度升高，都會重新推升損益兩平通膨率與央行利率預期。出口能力若能持續恢復，市場便更有理由認為週四的通膨壓力緩解可以延續。

食品價格是與能源並存、發展較慢的風險。聯合國食品商品指數已升至2022年底以來最高，乾旱、肥料限制、航運中斷及強烈聖嬰現象都威脅收成。摩根大通經濟學家預期，2027年上半年全球食品通膨將由2026年同期的2.8%升至5%。英國央行已把食品價格上行風險納入展望，費城聯準銀行調查也顯示企業預期未來價格壓力仍高。

初級信用市場近期有兩項定價考驗。CleanSpark的預期定價將顯示，投資人是否願意接受施工階段資料中心約8.5%的殖利率，即使項目有Meta的20年租約支持。CoreWeave的可轉債則會在發行量創紀錄、部分投資人已要求業者改善條件之際，測試市場對股權連結AI曝險的需求。

私募信貸案件的期限較遠，結果卻更為二元。Braskem債權人與股東須在10月9日前商定條款清單，決定誰提供新資金、誰承擔債務折價；Bathla管理人必須在潛在貸款買方要求大幅折價之際，取得範圍更大的融資方案；Emeria則須在債務到期日逼近、調整後與實際槓桿差異變得更重要前，證明預期AI節省能轉化為已實現的現金盈餘。

RBI在9月21日與28日進行的下兩次售債，將顯示5年期殖利率最初上升究竟是暫時調整，或是更大規模流動性驅動重新定價的開端。印度央行10月7日將進行政策檢討，交易員已預期升息25個基點。售債截止殖利率、銀行體系流動性、盧比與油價之間的互動，將決定緊縮是仍集中於殖利率曲線中段，或進一步擴散至整體國內融資條件。

對美債而言，眼前問題是週四的反彈能否承受勞動市場仍穩健、製造業價格正在上升的證據。10年期殖利率已回落至5%以下，但實質殖利率仍高，TIPS即使在2.653%的水準，標售需求仍然有限。油價進一步下跌及生產數據轉弱將支持債市；經濟活動強勁、能源壓力重現，或聯準會指引支持再升息數次，則會使近期觸及的多年殖利率高點重新進入視野。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries recovered sharply on Thursday as a second day of lower oil prices, the Bank of England’s retreat from long-dated gilt sales and confidence in the Federal Reserve’s inflation response interrupted the global bond selloff. The 10-year yield fell 9.2 basis points to 4.932%, ending an eight-session rise, while the 5-year led the rally with a 10.2-basis-point decline to 4.780%. The 2-year yield dropped 7.3 basis points to 4.665% and the 30-year fell 7.7 basis points to 5.285%.

The rally did not reverse the repricing toward tighter monetary policy. The 2s10s curve flattened another 1.9 basis points to 26.7, and the 2-year yield remained almost 49 basis points higher over the month after the Fed raised its target range to 3.75%-4% on Wednesday. Instead, the session showed investors distinguishing between additional short-rate increases and a loss of control over longer-run inflation. The 10-year real yield fell 7.1 basis points to 2.620%, while the 10-year breakeven declined 2.1 basis points to 2.312%.

Oil supplied immediate relief without ending the energy shock. Brent fell 1.65% to $104.08 and WTI declined 1.21% to $101.19 as Saudi Arabia sought to restore part of its East-West pipeline capacity. Both remained more than 14% higher over the month, leaving central banks sensitive to further pass-through into wages, food and underlying prices. The Treasury market nevertheless treated the day’s retreat as enough to reduce the inflation premium after the Fed’s unanimous increase had strengthened confidence that policymakers would respond if the shock persisted.

U.S. data complicated that relief. Initial jobless claims unexpectedly fell to 196,000 and the Philadelphia Fed’s manufacturing index remained well above expectations, with price measures rising. Housing construction weakened, however, while pending-home sales increased only slightly and remained almost 5% below their year-earlier level. The combination supported lower longer-term yields by exposing rate-sensitive weakness, but it offered little evidence that labor conditions or manufacturing demand had deteriorated enough to halt the Fed’s tightening cycle.

Demand was also uneven within the bond market. A $19 billion reopening of 10-year Treasury inflation-protected securities cleared at a 2.653% real yield, about 2 basis points above its pre-auction level, indicating a weak reception even as nominal Treasuries rallied. Corporate credit was firmer: U.S. high-yield spreads tightened modestly, Citigroup completed its largest dollar bond sale and Wells Fargo also attracted a large order book. The S&P 500 rose 1.14%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.73% and semiconductor shares climbed 3.14%, while the VIX fell almost 13%.

Britain delivered the clearest independent catalyst. The BOE held its policy rate at 3.75% and preserved the possibility of an increase if the energy shock lasts, but it paused active gilt sales until April and ended direct sales of long-dated securities. The 30-year gilt yield fell 12 basis points to 5.74%. That decision removed a source of duration supply without resolving the inflation problem, illustrating why the day’s bond recovery was substantial but conditional: central banks were tightening or threatening to tighten at the front end while trying to prevent balance-sheet policy and government issuance from unnecessarily aggravating pressure farther out.

## Treasuries Rally as Data Divide Labor, Prices and Housing

The Treasury recovery extended across maturities but was strongest in the intermediate sector. At 4.780%, the 5-year yield finished 10.2 basis points lower, compared with declines of 9.2 basis points at 10 years and 7.7 basis points at 30 years. The curve therefore retained the policy-led flattening created by the Fed decision rather than producing a large long-end steepening. The 2s30s spread narrowed 0.4 basis point to 62.0 and was 51.1 basis points flatter than a month earlier.

The daily move partly corrected the immediate post-Fed selloff. The central bank’s quarter-point increase had been expected, but Chair Kevin Warsh’s emphasis on persistent inflation and the median projection for another move this year drove the 10-year yield as high as 5.02% on Wednesday. On Thursday, lower crude prices and the gilt rally allowed investors to focus on the other side of the decision: a Fed viewed as willing to restrain inflation reduces the compensation required for an uncontrolled long-run price outcome, even if it raises the expected path of short rates.

Rate-option markets reinforced the distinction between a macroeconomic repricing and a disorderly Treasury event. Three-month options on 10-year rates implied about 79.5 basis points of annualized volatility, far below roughly 134 basis points when the 10-year yield approached 5% in October 2023. Options demand was more concentrated in short rates, where uncertainty over the Fed’s reaction function remained greater. That pattern was consistent with an orderly adjustment to stronger growth, fewer expected cuts and a higher long-run policy rate rather than a collapse in Treasury-market functioning.

The inflation decomposition also moved in a bond-friendly direction. The 10-year real yield fell to 2.620% and the breakeven declined to 2.312%. Lower oil helped both components: it reduced the near-term inflation impulse while making inflation protection less immediately attractive. The real yield nevertheless remained 18.2 basis points higher over the month, and the nominal 10-year was still 20.9 basis points above its level a month earlier. Thursday’s rally therefore eased, rather than erased, the tightening in financial conditions.

The 10-year TIPS auction showed the limits of that improvement. The $19 billion reopening drew a 2.653% yield, about 2 basis points above where the security traded immediately before the 1 p.m. bidding deadline. The result exceeded the previous auction’s 2.438% and was the highest since 2008, when inflation-protected securities were affected by financial-crisis liquidity stress. This time, the weak reception arrived as oil fell and investors contemplated further nominal rate increases, reducing the urgency of adding inflation protection despite the high real return.

The labor data gave the Fed little reason to retreat. Initial claims fell by 10,000 to a seasonally adjusted 196,000 in the week ended Sept. 12, below the 208,000 expected by economists and the lowest since mid-July. The four-week average declined by 2,750 to 203,250. Continuing claims dropped by 39,000 to 1.730 million in the week ended Sept. 5, below the 1.780 million consensus and the lowest since January 2024. Seasonal-adjustment distortions may have affected the readings, but the direction still indicated limited layoffs and a labor market capable of absorbing higher rates.

The Philadelphia Fed survey presented a different kind of resilience. Its September general-activity index fell to 37.8 from 47.4, but remained above the 30.5 consensus. New orders eased only slightly to 29.2 from 30.1, while shipments held at 27.7. The figures described slower expansion from an unusually strong August level rather than a contraction.

Employment softened more clearly. The survey’s employment index fell 16 points to 11.8, while the capital-expenditure index declined to 37.1 from 48.2. The future general-activity index dropped 21 points to 52.9. Those readings moderated the growth signal but remained positive, leaving the survey far from the type of broad deterioration that would ordinarily end a tightening cycle.

Price pressure moved in the opposite direction. The prices-paid index rose 8 points to 48.6, and prices received increased 14 points to 31.3, the highest since April. Future prices-paid and prices-received measures climbed to 71.3 and 72.3. Seventy-two percent of respondents identified labor supply as at least a slight constraint on capacity, up from 50% in June, while 36% expected energy-market constraints to worsen over the next three months. The combination of slower activity, continued expansion and firmer prices was precisely the mixture that complicates a rapid shift back toward easier policy.

Housing supplied the day’s clearer evidence of restraint. August housing starts fell 2.6% to an annualized 1.275 million, below the 1.310 million consensus, while the prior level was revised to 1.309 million. Building permits declined 2.7% to 1.394 million, compared with 1.410 million expected and 1.433 million previously. Starts were among the weakest since the pandemic, with multifamily construction responsible for much of the decline.

Pending sales of existing homes rose 0.3% in August, the first increase since May and better than the 0.1% decline expected in Bloomberg’s survey. The gain was weaker than the separate 2% consensus reported by Trading Economics and did not indicate a broad recovery. Contract signings were down 4.7% from a year earlier, compared with a 2.2% decline previously. Sales rose in the South and West but fell in the Midwest and Northeast.

Financing conditions continued to explain the divide. The average U.S. 30-year mortgage rate increased to 6.95% from 6.76%, and the 15-year rate rose to 6.26% from 6.09%. Pending transactions can advance despite those costs when buyers stop waiting for relief, but annual weakness and declining construction show how close-to-7% mortgages constrain affordability and project economics.

The releases therefore left the Fed with no single macroeconomic instruction. Claims and manufacturing prices supported continued vigilance; housing starts, permits and softer factory employment showed that restraint was already transmitting. The Treasury rally reflected that two-sided result. It reduced the probability that every strong headline would require an immediate additional increase, but it did not displace the broader conclusion that policy remains sensitive to persistent inflation and resilient labor demand.

## Britain Removes Long-Gilt Supply but Retains a Hiking Bias

The Bank of England kept Bank Rate at 3.75% for a sixth consecutive meeting, with six of nine Monetary Policy Committee members voting to hold. Catherine Mann, Megan Greene and Chief Economist Huw Pill preferred an immediate increase, repeating the 6-3 split from July. Their case was that acting before higher energy costs reach early-2027 wage settlements would reduce the risk of falling behind inflation.

Governor Andrew Bailey and the majority judged that the global energy shock had so far produced limited effects on domestic prices and wages. Their tolerance was conditional. Bailey said the longer the volatility persists, the greater the inflation impact and the more likely a rate increase becomes. The committee described inflation risks as more tilted to the upside than in July and expects price growth to reach about twice its 2% target early next year.

The BOE simultaneously acknowledged stronger activity. It raised its estimate for third-quarter growth to 0.4% after recent data exceeded expectations. That resilience reduces the immediate growth cost of another increase, but the committee also identified slack in the labor market, decelerating wage growth and unemployment near 5%. The result was a hold that preserved a tightening bias without endorsing the five quarter-point increases markets had priced at the peak of the week’s energy-driven selloff.

The larger market surprise came from the balance sheet. The BOE plans to unwind its £488 billion gilt portfolio by September 2034, but it paused all active sales until April 2027 and stopped direct sales of long-dated bonds. Gilts maturing from 2035 through 2049 may eventually be transferred to the Debt Management Office rather than sold directly into the market, subject to a final Treasury decision.

The proposed structure divides the portfolio into three broad parts. About £222 billion of bonds maturing by 2035 would be allowed to run off. The BOE would retain approximately £120 billion of gilts maturing in 2049 or later as assets backing banknotes in circulation. The remaining £146 billion due between 2035 and 2049 could be transferred or sold at about £20 billion a year through the DMO, which would have more flexibility to replace less-liquid securities with benchmark maturities that better match investor demand.

The change addressed a persistent source of pressure at the long end. The BOE estimates that quantitative tightening has added 20-30 basis points to 10-year government borrowing costs, while private estimates have placed the impact on 30-year yields higher. Pension demand for ultra-long securities has weakened, and the government’s own heavy issuance has made direct central-bank sales more difficult for the market to absorb.

Thirty-year gilt yields fell 12 basis points to 5.74%, the largest decline since May, after recently reaching their highest level since 1998. The 2-year yield declined 6 basis points to 4.70%. Traders reduced the probability of a November hike to about 85% and priced fewer than four increases over the following year.

The rally did not mean that balance-sheet relief had solved Britain’s inflation problem. The BOE expects higher food prices from a severe El Niño to add to the energy shock, and it warned that indirect effects may be delayed rather than absent. The government’s January energy-price-cap reset will transmit wholesale costs to households, while the timing overlaps with annual wage agreements. The committee’s three dissenters viewed that calendar as a reason to act before second-round effects become visible.

The policy-rate and gilt-supply decisions served different purposes. Holding the rate preserved room to assess domestic pass-through, while pausing sales reduced an avoidable source of duration pressure. The BOE did not lower borrowing costs through a new asset-purchase program or abandon its intention to shrink the portfolio. It changed the method and maturity composition of the unwind while keeping higher rates available if energy and food inflation spread.

The Treasury must still determine whether to accept the proposed DMO transfers. If implemented, the arrangement would consolidate public debt sales in the agency best able to choose liquid benchmarks and adjust duration. That could make Thursday’s long-end relief more durable than a temporary pause, although the government’s fiscal outlook and overall borrowing requirement remain independent sources of gilt supply.

## Credit Markets Absorb Bank and AI Financing

Corporate debt markets strengthened alongside Treasuries and equities. High-yield spreads tightened modestly, while distribution-adjusted total returns were positive across major funds: LQD gained about 0.68%, HYG 0.38%, JNK 0.37% and EMB 0.64%. The combination indicated broad participation in the bond rally rather than a move confined to government duration.

Citigroup used the improvement to raise $12 billion in its largest-ever U.S. dollar bond sale. The transaction attracted about $40 billion of peak orders, equivalent to roughly 3.3 times the final size. Demand for the longest maturity alone reached about $18 billion. Pricing on the 11-year note tightened to 93 basis points over the benchmark from initial discussions near 125 basis points.

The sale brought Citigroup’s dollar issuance for the year to $18.3 billion. The six largest U.S. banks have now raised a combined $177.3 billion in the investment-grade market, led by Goldman Sachs at $44 billion. Wells Fargo added a $6 billion sale in 4- and 11-year maturities on Thursday, drawing about $28 billion of peak demand.

The strength of the order books was notable because outright Treasury yields remained high. Borrowers benefited from the day’s government-bond rally and tighter credit risk premiums, but investors still received all-in yields well above those available during the low-rate period. Demand was particularly strong for longer bank maturities, which have become scarcer as many corporate issuers avoid locking in elevated funding costs for decades.

Artificial-intelligence infrastructure continued to generate more complicated financing. CoreWeave launched a $3 billion convertible-bond sale due in 2033, with an option to increase the transaction by $500 million. Initial coupon discussions were in a 2.375%-2.875% range. The company also established an at-the-market program allowing it to sell as many as 35 million shares.

The mix gives CoreWeave access to debt and equity-linked capital while limiting the immediate cash coupon relative to conventional unsecured debt. It also transfers part of the investor return to the future value of the company’s shares. The proceeds are intended for general corporate purposes, with a portion funding derivatives associated with the convertible offering.

CoreWeave’s transaction arrived after U.S.-listed companies raised a record $137.3 billion through convertibles this year. AI-related issuers have relied on that market, leveraged loans, private credit and asset-backed structures as the cost of data centers, chips and power connections exceeds the capacity of any single channel. Companies tied to AI infrastructure have borrowed about $419 billion globally this year, and signs of investor fatigue have already appeared. CoreWeave had to improve terms on a $2.6 billion leveraged loan in July.

CleanSpark tested a more conventional high-yield route. The company sought about $2.23 billion through a debut 5-year junk bond to finance a data center in Sandersville, Georgia. Initial yield discussions were around 8.5%, roughly 2 percentage points above the average yield on Bloomberg-tracked BB debt. Orders were approximately equal to the size of the offer when it was launched, a more restrained response than the multiple-times-covered bank deals.

The project is fully leased to Anviran, a Meta subsidiary, under a $6.6 billion, 20-year contract. Meta is expected to guarantee rent and operating expenses, and the data center is scheduled to start operating in Q4 2027. That commitment supplies a long-dated revenue stream, but bondholders must still absorb construction risk, the delay before operations begin and the financing needs of a company with a market value of about $3.29 billion.

The CleanSpark transaction is the first junk-bond offering linked to a Meta data center. Developers have sold roughly $39 billion of high-yield bonds this year, much of it backed by leases with large technology companies including Amazon and Oracle. The 8.5% initial discussion showed that contracted hyperscaler revenue can establish market access, but does not eliminate the premium required for a construction-stage, junk-rated project.

The contrast across the day’s deals was instructive. Citigroup and Wells Fargo attracted deep demand as established banks with liquid curves. CoreWeave reduced its cash coupon by offering equity participation. CleanSpark relied on a specific long-term lease but faced a meaningfully higher yield. Credit remained open, yet the terms reflected the borrower, collateral, construction status and path to cash flow rather than a single conclusion about enthusiasm for AI financing.

## Private Debt Stress Exposes Measurement and Valuation Gaps

The private-credit market produced a less benign picture, though even the scale of distress depended heavily on how defaults were defined. Fitch Ratings placed the default rate at a record 6.3%. Houlihan Lokey found a rate below 1% when loans were weighted by size, because the largest borrowers continued to perform. Pimco’s broader measure of “shadow” defaults among business-development companies reached 19%, up from about 14% in 2022.

Those figures describe different populations and events. Some measures count only missed payments or formal restructurings. Others include maturity extensions and payment-in-kind debt added after origination to relieve cash-flow pressure. Pimco’s calculation includes such “bad PIK,” on the view that replacing cash interest with additional debt can conceal deterioration even while a loan remains technically current.

The dispersion is important in a $1.8 trillion market with no comprehensive industry-wide dataset. European private loans tracked by Lincoln International had a default rate of 1.5%, partly because the measure excludes some restructurings captured elsewhere. Loan-size weighting also suppresses the influence of smaller borrowers, where distress has been more concentrated.

The question for investors is not only which number is correct, but whether losses and extensions are becoming large enough to impair returns. One industry estimate suggested managers could absorb default rates of 8%-9% as part of lending to highly leveraged companies, while rates approaching 12%-15% after a major shock could raise systemic concerns. Recovery values, collateral quality and the degree to which interest has actually been paid in cash matter alongside the headline count.

Bathla Group offered a concrete example of the valuation uncertainty. Centuria Bass Credit explored selling some debt tied to the insolvent Australian builder, but no transaction was imminent and potential buyers sought discounts of at least 20%-30%. Centuria Bass had disclosed A$278 million of Bathla exposure secured by six residential developments and temporarily paused redemptions from two funds as scrutiny increased.

Bathla owes about A$3.4 billion to creditors, much of it to private-credit funds, and entered voluntary administration in August after struggling to service its debt. Administrators secured approximately A$4 million of emergency financing and were seeking a broader package. The case is especially relevant to Australia’s A$200 billion private-credit sector because roughly half its assets are connected to real-estate development, where higher rates, construction costs and weaker sales can erode both cash flow and collateral value.

Creditors also challenged how corporate earnings are measured. French property-services company Emeria added €20 million of expected savings from a future artificial-intelligence program to its last-12-month EBITDA. Investors, lawyers and analysts said it was the first time they had seen prospective AI benefits used in that way.

Emeria said the adjustment was based on identified measures including automated document preparation, customer service, accounting and back-office work. The amount was not audited or reviewed by the company’s independent auditors and remains subject to change. The distinction is material because the company has about €3.5 billion of debt, shrinking earnings and approaching maturities.

Emeria reported leverage of roughly 8.44 times based on pro forma net debt and adjusted EBITDA. Excluding the AI item and several other adjustments totaling about €40 million, Bloomberg calculated the ratio at about 9.3 times. The sponsors were considering a potential €350 million cash injection as debt discussions continued. The disagreement was therefore not merely about accounting presentation: treating savings as already earned directly affected the leverage measure used to judge refinancing capacity.

Braskem’s restructuring talks showed how quickly a valuation dispute can become a contest over new money and control. Bondholders rejected the Brazilian petrochemical producer’s latest proposal as negotiations continued over an $11 billion debt burden. The plan called for creditors to provide about $2 billion of fresh financing, with roughly $1.25 billion used to repurchase existing debt at as little as 50% of face value and the remaining $750 million funding working capital.

Creditors objected to providing new capital without an enforceable contribution from shareholders Petrobras and IG4 Capital. Petrobras wants to avoid a bankruptcy filing but had not committed the type of binding equity support sought by bondholders. Some creditors were considering whether to withhold a counterproposal entirely, returning judicial reorganization to the center of discussions.

The parties have until Oct. 9 to agree on a term sheet and until late November to produce a final plan supported by more than half of creditors. Braskem’s dollar notes due in 2030 yielded about 26%, reflecting the probability that negotiations could move into court. The dispute turns on a substantive allocation of loss: creditors are being asked both to provide liquidity and to fund a discounted debt repurchase, while shareholders have not yet guaranteed the corresponding capital contribution.

Together, the cases exposed several forms of hidden leverage. Payment-in-kind restructurings can delay a recognized default; private loans may lack observable market prices until a sale is attempted; prospective AI savings can inflate earnings before they are realized; and restructuring proposals can label creditor money as rescue capital without settling the shareholder burden. High public-market issuance and tight broad spreads did not remove those borrower-specific weaknesses.

## Global Policy and Sovereign Funding Remain Restrictive

India’s central bank completed the first tranche of a liquidity withdrawal that had already unsettled the local curve. The Reserve Bank of India sold 500 billion rupees, about $5.2 billion, of government securities maturing from fiscal 2029 through fiscal 2032. It was the RBI’s first auction-based net open-market bond sale since November 2017.

Cutoff yields were slightly above market estimates. The 5-year yield rose as much as 6 basis points to 6.83% after the result, compared with an increase of as much as 3 basis points in the benchmark 10-year yield. The relative move reflected the concentration of the operation in maturities that are sensitive to banking-system liquidity as well as expectations for an October policy-rate increase.

The sale removed close to 0.2% of banking-system deposits. Surplus liquidity had reached a record 11.6 trillion rupees on Sept. 6 before declining to about 7.4 trillion rupees through tax payments and foreign-exchange intervention. The RBI plans 2 additional 250 billion-rupee sales on Sept. 21 and Sept. 28, completing the announced 1 trillion-rupee program. ICICI Securities Primary Dealership estimated that about 2 trillion rupees could ultimately be withdrawn through bond sales during the tightening cycle.

India’s operation added duration supply at the same time as the central bank drained cash, making it more consequential than a temporary liquidity tool. Traders widely expected a 25-basis-point rate increase in October, while oil above $100 added to imported-inflation pressure. The result reinforced a global pattern in which central banks were addressing inflation through both policy rates and balance sheets, although the BOE was simultaneously adjusting its balance-sheet method to reduce long-end disruption.

The Czech National Bank unanimously held its benchmark rate at 3.75% after June’s first increase in four years. Governor Ales Michl said the earlier hike had tightened conditions sufficiently for now, but left the next meeting as a choice between another increase and an unchanged rate. Core inflation remained elevated, and officials were monitoring services, housing, wages, government spending and oil.

Forward-rate markets priced about two additional quarter-point increases by year-end and four over the following 12 months. Michl declined to endorse that path, but said the board would tighten again if inflation risks materialized. The November meeting is therefore live despite August headline inflation remaining below target.

The European Central Bank’s public debate was similarly focused on whether an energy shock that has not yet produced a wage-price spiral will require further action. Irish central-bank Governor Gabriel Makhlouf said every meeting, including Oct. 29, remained live. He saw no concerning wage pass-through but emphasized that inflation was still above the ECB’s 2% objective and that energy risks remained on the upside.

Finland’s Olli Rehn also found no clear second-round effects, noting that the labor market was less tight than in 2022. He nevertheless said the shock was not over and that upward risks could still emerge. Rehn warned against broad government subsidies that dilute price signals and supported temporary, targeted assistance instead. He also pointed to the ECB’s transmission tools as available if political or sovereign-market stress interferes with policy, while saying no intervention was currently necessary.

Croatian central-bank Governor Ante Zigman placed greater emphasis on the cost of failing to contain inflation. With euro-area inflation above 3% and Q2 growth stronger than expected, he argued that uncontrolled price pressure would eventually endanger expansion. He agreed that wage and other second-round effects remained contained, leaving October dependent on new data rather than current market expectations for at least three further increases.

Europe also confronted a longer-term funding question as the European Commission sought broader index inclusion for common EU debt. About €800 billion of EU bonds are outstanding, making the market the second-largest AAA debt pool in Europe and the third-largest globally. Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis argued that their exclusion from major sovereign benchmarks limits demand and secondary-market liquidity even though the securities already receive sovereign-equivalent treatment as collateral at clearing houses and in ECB refinancing operations.

Index inclusion could become more important as EU issuance expands to finance defense and the next long-term budget. The policy would not reduce the amount of borrowing, but could widen the eligible investor base and improve the securities’ liquidity relative to national sovereign curves. Rehn separately supported jointly issued European defense debt, connecting the market-structure initiative with prospective supply.

Canada documented the higher cost of sovereign financing through a C$3 billion auction of bonds due June 1, 2059. The securities cleared at an average yield of 4.201%, the highest at a Canadian 30-year auction since July 2007. Canadian yields remained below U.S. levels, but fuel-driven inflation pressure and the international rise in term premiums pushed long borrowing costs higher.

Japan showed a possible shift in who might absorb that supply. Retail sales of Japanese government bonds rose 84% from a year earlier to a record ¥5.14 trillion between April and September. Households hold about ¥1,132 trillion in cash and deposits, while government bonds account for only around 1.9% of that amount. If the share returned to its 2008 peak of 4.5%, it could imply an additional ¥28.5 trillion of purchases, equal to about 22% of annual JGB issuance.

That potential demand matters as the BOJ reduces purchases and higher domestic yields compete with overseas bonds. The Ministry of Finance plans to broaden eligibility for retail JGBs to nonprofit entities and small unlisted companies, while proposals include admitting government bonds to tax-advantaged investment accounts and exempting some holdings from inheritance tax. Retail demand cannot replace institutional buyers immediately, but it offers a larger domestic funding pool as Japanese rates normalize.

Emerging-market sovereign performance remained selective rather than uniformly weak. Mozambique’s and Senegal’s dollar bonds returned 3% and 2.2% respectively during the month, compared with a 1.23% loss for a broader emerging-market bond index. Mozambique’s 2031 eurobond yield fell 76 basis points in September to 10.43%, its lowest since April 2022, as investors responded to IMF discussions, talks with China over debt rescheduling and preliminary approaches from bondholders.

Senegal sought IMF board approval for a $2.2 billion program. Its bonds stabilized after officials clarified that debt service would continue for now and paid the coupon on securities due in 2048. Both countries still face unresolved debt-sustainability work, but progress toward official financing provided an issuer-specific source of support while developed-market yields were rising.

## Forward Market Significance

The Bank of Japan’s Sept. 18 decision is the nearest global policy test. All economists in Bloomberg’s survey expect an increase from 1.00% to 1.25%, the second hike in three months and the shortest interval between BOJ increases since 1990. With the move almost fully priced, Governor Kazuo Ueda’s 3:30 p.m. press conference will carry more information than the rate itself.

The central question is whether Ueda presents September as a one-time acceleration or keeps the door open to another move by January. A rate of 1.25% would enter the lower end of the BOJ’s estimated neutral range. Continued language that financial conditions remain accommodative would indicate that officials still see room to tighten, while opposition from recently appointed board members Toichiro Asada or Ayano Sato would raise questions about the breadth of support.

The yen was near 156 per dollar before the decision after weakening as much as 1% following the Fed’s hike. Strategists identified the 158-158.50 area as a likely test if the BOJ’s communication is interpreted as dovish, with 160 possible over time if U.S. rates rise faster than Japanese rates. Reduced speculative yen shorts and the demonstrated willingness of Japan and the U.S. to intervene jointly could restrain the move, but a quarter-point hike alone may not narrow the expected policy gap enough to support the currency.

U.S. industrial production and manufacturing output on Sept. 18 will extend the domestic activity test beyond Thursday’s regional and housing data. Both monthly measures are expected to rise 0.3%, after 0.2%, while capacity utilization is forecast to increase to 76.4% from 76.3%. A strong result would reinforce the Fed’s view that the economy can withstand additional restraint; weakness would add to the evidence from housing starts, permits and softer Philadelphia Fed employment.

Governor Michelle Bowman’s scheduled remarks will provide the first named Fed assessment after the unanimous increase and the subsequent claims, manufacturing and housing releases. Markets need to determine whether officials share the more aggressive path reflected in trading or remain closer to the median projection of one further move this year. The distinction matters especially at the front end, where option demand indicates greater uncertainty than in longer rates.

Oil remains the most immediate cross-market condition. Saudi Arabia’s effort to restore about half the capacity of its East-West pipeline within days helped Brent close below $105, but WTI and Brent remained above $100 and Middle Eastern supplies were still constrained. Delays, additional attacks or renewed U.S.-Iran escalation would restore pressure on breakevens and central-bank expectations. A sustained restoration of export capacity would give markets more reason to treat Thursday’s inflation relief as durable.

Food prices create a slower-moving risk beside energy. A United Nations food-commodity index has reached its highest level since late 2022, while drought, fertilizer constraints, shipping disruptions and a strong El Niño threaten harvests. JPMorgan economists expect global food inflation to reach 5% in H1 2027 from 2.8% in the corresponding period of 2026. The BOE has already incorporated upside food risk into its outlook, and the Philadelphia Fed survey showed businesses expecting future price pressure to remain high.

Primary credit markets face two near-term execution tests. CleanSpark’s expected pricing will show whether investors accept an approximately 8.5% yield for a construction-stage data center backed by a 20-year Meta lease. CoreWeave’s convertible sale will test demand for equity-linked AI exposure after record issuance and signs that some investors require improved terms from the sector.

The private-credit cases have longer deadlines but more binary outcomes. Braskem’s creditors and shareholders have until Oct. 9 to agree on a term sheet determining who supplies fresh capital and who bears the debt discount. Bathla’s administrators must secure a broader financing package while potential loan buyers demand substantial markdowns. Emeria must demonstrate whether its proposed AI savings become realized cash earnings before looming maturities make the distinction between adjusted and actual leverage more consequential.

India’s next two RBI bond sales on Sept. 21 and Sept. 28 will show whether the initial rise in 5-year yields was a temporary adjustment or the beginning of a larger liquidity-driven repricing. The central bank’s Oct. 7 policy review follows, with traders already expecting a quarter-point increase. The interaction among bond-sale cutoffs, banking-system liquidity, the rupee and oil will determine whether tightening remains concentrated in the intermediate curve or spreads more broadly through domestic financing conditions.

For Treasuries, the immediate issue is whether Thursday’s recovery can survive evidence that the labor market remains firm and manufacturing prices are rising. The 10-year yield has moved back below 5%, but its real component remains high and the TIPS auction showed limited demand even at 2.653%. Further declines in oil and softer production would support the rally. Strong activity, renewed energy pressure or Fed guidance validating several additional increases would put the recent multiyear yield highs back into view.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries snap an 8-session selloff as oil retreats and the BOE removes long-gilt supply
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries recovered across maturities, led by a 10.2-basis-point decline in the 5-year yield to 4.780%. The 10-year yield fell 9.2 basis points to 4.932%, ending an 8-session rise, while the 2-year dropped 7.3 basis points to 4.665% and the 30-year declined 7.7 basis points to 5.285%. Lower oil prices and confidence that the Fed would respond to persistent inflation reduced the premium for an uncontrolled long-run price outcome, but the 2s10s curve flattened to 26.7 basis points and the 2-year yield remained almost 49 basis points higher over the month.

Brent fell 1.65% to $104.08 and WTI declined 1.21% to $101.19 as Saudi Arabia sought to restore part of its East-West pipeline capacity. The relief remained conditional because both benchmarks were still more than 14% higher over the month. Initial jobless claims fell unexpectedly and Philadelphia Fed price measures rose, while weaker housing starts, permits and factory employment showed that higher rates were restraining sensitive parts of the economy without yet ending the tightening case.

The BOE supplied the clearest independent catalyst by holding Bank Rate at 3.75% while pausing active gilt sales until April 2027 and ending direct sales of long-dated bonds. The 30-year gilt yield fell 12 basis points to 5.74%. Corporate credit also strengthened, with modestly tighter U.S. high-yield spreads and large bank order books, although a weak 10-year TIPS auction and borrower-specific stress in private debt showed that the rally did not remove financing and valuation risks.
